title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: Uganda as many other countries faces challenges in addressing gender-based violence (GBV) and ensuring workplace safety, particularly for women. To strengthen the institutional capacity of employers' organizations, the ILO collaborates with the Federation of Uganda Employers (FUE) to advance organizational resilience, promote gender equality, and foster decent work. Key initiatives include developing tools and training programs to integrate risk management practices into FUE’s strategic operations. These efforts support Ugandan companies in adopting improved workplace safety practices, establishing grievance mechanisms, and implementing leadership programs like the Female Future Programme (FFP). Additionally, FUE organizes sensitization meetings to address sexual and reproductive health rights, combat sexual harassment, and curb GBV. The intervention complements national efforts following Uganda’s ratification of ILO Convention 190 (C-190) on Violence and Harassment. It aligns with the amended Employment Bill (2023), which strengthens protections for employees. By enhancing capacity for risk identification and mitigation, this initiative empowers FUE to provide sustainable services to its members, address emerging challenges, and promote equitable and inclusive business practices. This CPO contributes to Sustainable Development Goals 8, 4, and 5, focusing on economic growth, skills development, and gender equality. The outcomes aim to improve workplace conditions, strengthen FUE’s governance, and bolster its role as a champion for workplace safety and equity in Uganda.
